newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota corn harvest makes little progress.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota corn harvest makes little progress.

text.p: South Dakota's corn harvest made meager progress during the week ended November 24 as ice and snow on the plants limited harvest activity, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Warmer temperatures are needed to melt the ice and snow before harvesting can be completed. Some sorghum and sunflowers also remained unharvested, the report said.
Corn harvested was 93 percent versus 91 a week ago, 98 a year ago, and the five-year average of 88 percent.
Winter wheat was rated 70 percent good to excellent, 21 percent fair, six percent poor and three percent very poor, the report said.
More producers began feeding their cattle hay and silage as cattle were being removed from cornstalks and pastures covered with snow.
Feed supplies were rated three percent surplus, 95 percent adequate and two percent short, the report said.
